It separates vision-, text-, and audio-driven tasks, compares representative architectures, discusses language-model-assisted planning, and catalogs datasets and evaluation practices.
conditions: Reviewed conditions include reference images/videos, human pose, text, speech, and music across portrait animation, dance, talking-head, try-on, and holistic-body video tasks. The paper reviews conditioning interfaces rather than presenting a new jointly trained controllable 3D motion generator.
data_split: Not applicable: this is a literature review with no newly trained model and no train/test split. Dataset tables summarize external benchmarks; their subjects, recording protocols, and partitions are heterogeneous. No reproducible systematic-review search query, screening flow, or meta-analysis protocol is specified.
metrics: No new experimental metric is introduced. Section VI catalogs pixel/perceptual quality measures such as PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS and FID; temporal/video measures such as FVD; alignment and task-specific pose/lip/identity scores, plus broader video-quality benchmarks.
evaluation: Taxonomy figures and method tables compare capabilities and pipeline stages; Section VI inventories 64 publicly available human-video datasets and explains evaluation families. These are structured literature summaries, not controlled reruns or an aggregated numerical leaderboard under one common protocol.
evidence_locator: §I scope/taxonomy, §III motion planning, §IV modality-based generation, §V refinement/output, §VI/Figure 11 and Table VIII (metrics/datasets), §VII challenges.

title: RealisMotion: Decomposed Human Motion Control and Video Generation in the World Space
summary: RealisMotion separates subject appearance, background video, world-space trajectory, and action. A ground-aware coordinate system, focal-length calibration, trajectory unprojection, speed alignment, and orientation adjustment edit 3D motion. Wan-based video diffusion injects subject tokens, background channels, and added motion control signals.
limitations: Estimated depth, camera calibration, body recovery, and 3D-to-video alignment remain error sources. Internal training data limit reproducibility. Visually consistent world-space animation does not establish accurate contact, object dynamics, or robot executability; cross-domain characters are demonstrations rather than comprehensive controlled evaluation.
method: RealisMotion separates subject appearance, background video, world-space trajectory, and action. A ground-aware coordinate system, focal-length calibration, trajectory unprojection, speed alignment, and orientation adjustment edit 3D motion. Wan-based video diffusion injects subject tokens, background channels, and added motion control signals.
conditions: A reference subject image, background video, trajectory and action controls, with optional text/face cues. Actions may come from a motion bank or text-to-motion generator. An image-to-video variant merges subject/background and consequently loses their independent customization.
data_split: Finetunes Wan-2.1 14B on an internal approximately 3,300-hour video collection. Evaluates trajectory/orientation on a newly assembled 100-video Trajectory100 set and action on RealisDance-Val. Exact training/validation partition proportions and source-identity grouping are not reported in the inspected setup.
metrics: Translation error in meters and rotation error in degrees measure recovered trajectory/orientation agreement. PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS assess image fidelity/perception; FID and FVD assess image/video feature-distribution mismatch. These are video-control metrics rather than physical human-object motion scores.
evaluation: Table 2 compares trajectory control with Wan, Tora, and RealisDance-DiT; Table 3 evaluates action control. Table 4 ablates calibration, body-hand matching, text, extra face input, positional encoding, and random masking. Subject/background customization is largely illustrated qualitatively.
evidence_locator: §3 decomposed 3D editing/video injection; §§4.1–4.3, Tables 2–4; supplementary training details and depth-error robustness analysis.
